The exact positive identity B^2-AD=k(N-k)/[N^2(N-1)] and a(q) strictly decreasing prove the unique threshold and endpoint equality. Strictly decreasing B^2/D in excitation count and explicit first-order asymptotic expansions establish both scaling profiles and the critical occupancy. An extracted independent verifier checks rational identities, explicit Kraus channels, and spin-flip eigenvalues. No finite test is treated as the all-N proof.

value.rationale: The excitation number is an operationally natural index of the many-qubit Dicke state. The exact square-root excitation threshold distinguishes states with persistent pairwise entanglement from ones with genuine finite-loss sudden death; a second macroscopic-occupancy regime has a sharply vanishing 1/N lifetime. Universal scaling functions quantify the crossover and make a motivated dimension-dependent comparison to the pre-existing multipartite Bell nonlocality loss question, rather than an arbitrary isolated X-state example.
